newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ERA says outlook brightest since '81.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ERA says outlook brightest since '81.

text.p: Uranium miner Energy Resources of Australia Ltd said on Thursday that its production outlook was the brightest for 15 years, with the recent hike in international uranium oxide prices allowing the company to proceed with new capital investment.

"The rapid increase in the market price for uranium over the last two years from US$9.25 per pound to US$16.50 per pound has meant the supply of uranium from Ranger (in the Northern Territory) is now a more profitable option for the company," chairman Campbell Anderson said at the annual meeting.
"We expect that this will continue for at least the forseeable future," Anderson said.
He did not forecast 1996/97 profits but said the company had achieved its 1995/96 target of improved profitability along with securing new contracts, particularly in the United States.

"The company believes the outlook for uranium production in Australia is the brightest for over 15 years," Anderson said, noting Australia was forecast to account for 12 percent or 9,000 tonnes of oxide by the year 2000 against seven percent now.

He said the company would start further exploration work on the Jabiluka 2 orebody next year, which he described as ERA's largest and richest orebody with current reserves of 90,400 tonnes of oxide. The orebody was still open at depth.

Anderson said a draft environmental impact statement was opened for public comment on Thursday for a period of three months. He said the draft statement forecast that the Jabiluka project, located in the Northern Territory's Kakadu National Park, would contribute A$3.5 billion of benefits to the Australian community and A$6.2 billion to gross domestic product. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
